chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from some of his men, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Isa ibn Sulayman, from Bakkar ibn Kardam, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man meets a woman and says to her, 'Marry yourself to me for a month,' without specifying the exact month, then he leaves and meets her again after years. He said: 'He has her for that month if he specified it, and if he did not specify it, there is no way for him to claim her.' And whenever he contracted a mut'ah (temporary marriage) with her for a single time in an unspecified manner, the contract is permanent, indicating that.

key_terms.زَوِّجِينِي نَفْسَكَ: Marry yourself to me (proposal of marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on temporary marriage if the duration is not specifically named?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the ambiguity in temporary marriage contracts where the duration is mentioned but not specified; if the man later claims her after years without having specified the month, he has no right to her unless he had previously specified it. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that an unspecified duration in a mut'ah contract defaults to permanence (daim), distinguishing it from a fixed-term temporary marriage. The hadith underscores the importance of precise specification (takhis) in mut'ah to ensure the contract remains temporary rather than converting into a permanent union.
